title: The Race for ChatGPT Advertising has Begun. Get a Head Start with Sprinklr.
summary: Buyers are asking ChatGPT, not searching. Learn why ChatGPT ads matter now and how Sprinklr lets you run them with the governance of every other channel.
body_markdown:
Somewhere right now, a buyer is typing something into ChatGPT that would never fit in a search bar:


*We're a 400-person fintech, our sales team hates our current CRM, we need something that plays nicely with slack and doesn't take six months to roll out. What should we be looking at?*


And since February of this year, your brand can show up alongside ChatGPT’s response even if your website isn’t[optimized for AEO](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/5-reasons-for-you-to-start-optimizing-for-aeo/) .

##


The quiet shift in how people decide


For two decades, discovery had a shape you could plan around. A keyword. A results page. A bid. Your entire paid playbook was built on the assumption that people express intent in fragments, and you reverse-engineer the rest.


That assumption is dissolving in real time. ChatGPT has 1 billion **** weekly active users. And roughly[one in five](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/emmalouisewilson_about-20-of-chatgpt-conversations-carry-activity-7492590592061755392-1yq_#:~:text=About%2020%25%20of%20ChatGPT%20conversations%20carry%20shopping%20intent%2C%20according%20to%20OpenAI%27s%20own%20data.) of those conversations carries shopping intent.


So what actually changes when a query becomes a conversation? Intent gets richer.


A three-word search hides the objective, the constraints and the trade-offs a buyer is weighing. A ChatGPT prompt, on the other hand, lays all three on the table. People don't type their budget into Google but they do take the time to share that information with ChatGPT.


##


Why this channel matters now, not next year


ChatGPT Ads let brands appear within ChatGPT conversations at the moment someone is researching, comparing, and choosing.


Not while they're passively scrolling. While they're deciding.


The mechanics are deliberately simple. There primary ad format contains an image, a title, body copy, and a destination URL.


[Source](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001207-ads-in-chatgpt-the-basics#ad-format)


Targeting is contextual rather than demographic. You use context hints to define the types of conversations your ads should appear in, and you target or exclude by country. Every ad passes through OpenAI's review process after publication.


According to[EMARKETER](https://www.emarketer.com/content/ai-search-ad-spending-will-climb-with-consumer-adoption) , U.S. AI-search ad spend will reach $26 billion by 2029, **** up from roughly $1.1 billion in 2025.


Whether that number lands exactly there is beside the point. The direction is unmistakable, and every emerging channel teaches the same lesson: the brands that build presence before inventory crowds and costs climb are the ones that own the category later.


What does that mean? When your buyers ask an AI instead of a search engine, the brands absent from that answer aren't losing[share of voice (SOV)](https://www.sprinklr.com/blog/share-of-voice/) . They're invisible.


**4 reasons why brands cannot ignore ChatGPT Ads**


1. **Richer intent signals:** A ChatGPT prompt reveals a prospect’s objective, constraints, and tradeoffs better than a traditional search query
2. **Real-time reach:** Ads show up in real time as decision-makers research, compare, and choose as opposed to after the fact
3. **First-mover advantage:** Early adopters build sustainable presence and stay top-of-mind in buying situations before competitors, eventually, start to crowd the space
4. **High discoverability:** When a buyer turns to AI instead of traditional search, brands absent in the resulting answer stay hidden from the buyer’s radar


***NOTE:*** *Before you build a media plan on that 1 billion figure: ads in ChatGPT currently reach users on the Free and Go plans only, so the ad-eligible audience is a subset of the total user base. Still enormous. Just not the whole number.*


##


The part nobody puts on the launch slide


Here's what your paid media team already knows: every new channel arrives the same way. Thrilling on the pitch, expensive in practice.


Another login. Another naming convention nobody follows. Another set of metrics living in another dashboard, reconciled manually at the end of the month. Another place a campaign can go live without the right approval, the right creative or the right compliance check attached.


So what does it really cost to add a channel? Not the media spend. The operational cost — the one that shoots up every quarter, that no one budgets for, that shows up as slower launches, inconsistent reporting, and a governance gap wide enough for a brand-safety incident to walk through.


Layer that on top of a channel where nobody can yet tell you what a good CPC looks like, and the brands treating ChatGPT Ads as one more disconnected experiment wouldn't just struggle to scale it but have a hard time even reading it.


That's the real question behind ChatGPT Ads. NOT should you be there. The question is whether you can be there with enough discipline to learn something from it without rebuilding your operation to do it.
